title: 一边…一边…: while doing
summary: Lets you say someone does two things at the same time, as in 他一边吃饭一边看电视.
structure: Subject + 一边 + Verb A + 一边 + Verb B
explanation:
一边 A 一边 B means doing A and B at the same time: 他一边吃饭一边看电视 'He eats while watching TV.' Put 一边 before EACH verb. The subject comes first, only once.

Both actions should be things one person can do at once (listening and writing, walking and talking). For one action at a point in time, use …的时候 instead.

examples.zh: 他一边吃饭一边看电视。
我喜欢一边听歌一边跑步。
examples.en: I like listening to music while running.

examples.zh: 她一边笑一边说：'太好了！'
不要一边开车一边打电话。
examples.en: Don't talk on the phone while driving.

mistakes.right: 他一边吃饭一边看电视。
mistakes.why: Use 一边 before each of the two verbs.

mistakes.wrong: 一边他吃饭，一边他看电视。
mistakes.right: 他一边吃饭一边看电视。
mistakes.why: The subject comes first, once; 一边 goes before the verbs.

why: Correct: 一边 before each verb.
然后 means 'then' — one after another, not at the same time.
和 links nouns, not two actions.

exercises.why: Subject + 一边 A + 一边 B.

why: The second verb needs 一边 too.
The subject goes before the first 一边.

exercises.instruction: Say he does both at the same time.
options: 他一边喝咖啡一边看书。
他喝咖啡一边看书一边。
一边他喝咖啡，一边他看书。
why: 一边 goes before each verb, not after.
Say the subject once, at the start.

options: 不要一边开车一边打电话。
一边不要开车一边打电话。
why: Correct: 不要 + 一边 A 一边 B.
不要 goes before the whole pattern.

exercises.en: I like listening to music while running.
why: Correct: the first verb also needs 一边.
